newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. repatriates Rwandan refugees from east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. repatriates Rwandan refugees from east Zaire.

text.p: Rwandan Hutu refugees left eastern Zaire by truck on Thursday for Rwanda as aid agencies struggled to reach 80,000 more scattered deeper in the Zairean interior.
Filippo Grandi, east Zaire representative of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), said 4,800 refugees were repatriated by trucks from Karuba west of Goma on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"The Karuba repatriation is continuing today but we expect it to be a bit slower because of logistic problems," he told Reuters in the eastern city of Goma on the border with Rwanda.
He said the last refugees at Amisi and Tingi Tingi farther to the west were repatriated by air on Tuesday including some unaccompanied children taken to a transit centre in Goma city.

In the northeastern Zairean capital of Kisangani, UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg said a train left with a medical team to investigate problems at kilometre 82 (mile 50) south of the city where refugees are in horrific condition.
UNHCR says almost half of the 800 Rwandan and Burundian refugees who gathered at kilometre 82 in mid-March have died of malnutrition, malaria, other illnesses and infected wounds.
Stromberg said the medical team would give first aid and check the possibility of evacuating refugees from kilometre 82 by train to kilometre 40 (mile 25) south of the city.
"We need to get them to kilometre 40 where we can help them," said Stromberg by telephone. "They need hospitalisation but so many are in such bad shape it is hard to move them."
Aid agencies say they are struggling against restrictions imposed by the rebels, who oppose the formation of any refugee camps, bad weather and dreadful roads to bring aid to groups of refugees.
In Geneva, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) joined calls by other aid agencies for the rebels to give unrestricted access to the thousands of Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees.
The Swiss-run ICRC said in a statement the displaced Rwandans were in a disastrous state and that any new forced movement could lead to the deaths of thousands of refugees.

"With the arrival of heavy rains in areas with dense vegetation, the scale of needs has become alarming. It is no longer a matter of feeding the hungry but of coping with serious medical emergencies," the Geneva-based agency said.
It said the rebels limited the distribution of aid to refugee assembly points along the railway line south of Kisangani and had forced back those who reached the outskirts of the city.
The Tutsi-dominated rebels ordered some 20,000 refugees on Monday to leave a site seven km (four miles) south of Kisangani and move farther south, citing security reasons.
The rebels say they are concerned the refugees include Hutu former Rwandan troops and militiamen who had leading roles in Rwanda's 1994 genocide and have fought alongside Zaire's army.
There are an estimated 80,000 refugees 26 to 82 km (16 to 50 miles) in groups along a railway line south of Kisangani.

U.N. aid officials said the rebels were allowing aid workers to reach the refugees but did not want the Rwandans to stay where they were until they could recover enough to move on and would not allow them via Kisangani to be repatriated by air.
Some 200,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees are unaccounted for since they left their camps near the borders with Rwanda and Burundi at the start of the rebel campaign in October last year.
